claim: 1 000 runs is the number Arcuri and Briand recommend for randomised algorithms.
quote: On each artefact in the case study, run each randomized algorithm at least n D1000 times.
locator: Sec. 11 'Practical guidelines', p. 244 (printed; PDF p. 26); also Sec. 8, pp. 236-237
issue: The number holds. The source states it as a floor ('at least'), in a software-engineering setting (search-based testing); 'the number recommended' reads it as a target, a small softening that does not change the claim's use here.

claim: Running each configuration on 1 000 seeds meets the source's recommendation.
quote:
On each artefact in the case study, run each randomized algorithm at least n D1000 times. ... When a large number of artefacts can be used in the case study (e.g. for unit testing of open
source software) but there are constraints in terms of execution time, then it is advisable to
execute less runs per artefact (although at least n D 10) and use more artefacts
issue: The recommendation is 1 000 runs per artefact (problem instance). Here each seed generates its own network (U0603), so every network gets one run per configuration: 1 000 artefacts x 1 run, which is neither the source's 1 000-per-artefact rule nor its many-artefacts fallback (at least 10 runs each). The match holds only if the network draw is read as part of the algorithm's randomness rather than as the artefact. The sentence should own that reading, or an examiner can say the guideline is misapplied.
fix_text: is run on the same 1 000 seeds, the number of runs recommended for randomised algorithms \citep{arcuri2014hitchhiker}, here with the network drawn as part of each run.

claim: Table 5.1: 1 000 runs per configuration, sourced to Arcuri and Briand.
quote:

issue: Number supported (Sec. 11 gives n = 1000 explicitly). Same per-artefact caveat as U0602 applies to the table cell.
